messages.author: c78a1f7a72c7aa42
messages.subject: proxying shiny via nginx ?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to set up a front-end to shiny via nginx
(shiny-server cannot be used in this setup, for licensing reasons).

I have a shiny app (like the 01_hello example) running on port 8888.

The nginx setup has the corresponding definition:

        server {
            server_name helloapp.example.com;
            location / {
                proxy_pass http://localhost:8888;
                proxy_http_version 1.1;
                proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
                proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
                proxy_set_header Host $host;
            }
        }

(as per http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/websocket.html -- yes, recent nginx versions can proxy websockets)

The observed behavior, when connecting to http://helloapp.example.com is that I see the app, everything (html, css and js files) gets transferred OK, but immediately the whole page becomes grey.

Looking at the css, the grey background means "disconnected" and gets applied (only?) when the socket is closed.
The websocket gets proxied, because by observing in the Chrome developer tools I see the Upgrade message, and it seems that some data have made it through (I see two frames):
{"method":"init","data":{"obs":500,".shinyout_distPlot_width":928,".shinyout_distPlot_height":400,"__allowDataUriScheme":true}}
{"method":"update","data":{".shinyout_distPlot_width":928,".shinyout_distPlot_height":400}}

But, as described, almost immediately the websocket is closed and the whole page goes into "disconnected" state.

Does anyone have any ideas?
Has anyone achieved anything similar by other means (i.e., 'hiding" the shiny web app) ?

Many thanks in advance for any input,

-- zvr -

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: proxying shiny via nginx ?
parts:
Did you copy the "map" portion of the nginx conf example as well? (I don't know if it matters)

You are probably aware of the downsides of this approach, notably that unless you take precautions the R process may exit and leave the app inaccessible until you restart it.

If Shiny Server's AGPL license is the only thing stopping you from using it, feel free to contact me offline, we may be able to work out a dual license.

messages.author: cb0312e9c60a7720
messages.subject: Re: proxying shiny via nginx ?
parts:
I have the similar issue.
In my case nginx + shiny-server open source.
app is loading fine, when I initiate one of the heavier processes by click on actionButton (fetch 6k rows from db, calc 6 series of statistics - 6k rows each - plot them using rChartsDygraphs) I get the grey app with "disconnected" div in around 30% times. It occurs much more often if I switch to another tab for time of the processing (using chrome). Full processing takes less than 10 seconds.
I was able to see there is websocket error in the js console. Disabling websocket remove that error in js console, but doesn't fix the issue.
Already tried:
app_init_timeout 
app_idle_timeout 
disable_websockets true;
None of the above helps.

Joe Cheng - what do you mean by "map" portion of the nginx?

Regards,
Jan

Me too.

I have Shiny server open source (1.2.0.360) behind haproxy (1.5.0). Processing time on the server does not seem to play a role, but client side processing does. Whenever page rendering takes a few seconds (e.g. due to big tables) the page greys out after the browser is done with rendering. This does not happen when using shiny server directly, without proxy.

Best

Thomas
